text:
maria-g: Hey folks, noticed model-puller pods in us-west2 failing to download blobs from the model registry (503 / connection reset). started ~06:10 UTC, spike in failed model loads.
keith-infra: Looking now. Is this all GPU cluster pods or just the new spot pool?
maria-g: All pools in the cluster, both spot and ondemand. curl to the registry LB times out from the pods but works from bastion.
opsbot: Alert: high failure-rate on /v1/models/download from inference-us-west2 (rate 52/min) -- SLI breach threshold crossed.
jonathan: Can you paste a failing curl + tcpdump snippet?
maria-g: Sure, from a failing pod: ```kubectl exec -n inference model-puller-7f8c -- curl -vS --max-time 10 https://models.internal.redwood/v1/artifact/abc123```
maria-g: curl output: ```* Connected to models.internal.redwood (10.8.4.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* Connection reset by peer```
keith-infra: tcpdump shows SYN from pod src 10.100.12.34:52344 -> dst 10.8.4.12:443 then SYN,ACK from 10.8.4.12:443 -> 10.100.12.34:52344 but the SYN,ACK never reaches pod. Looks like return path blocked.
devin-ml: That smells like a NACL or SG asymmetry. Any recent infra changes? terraform?
keith-infra: There's one change in last deploy: tightening of edge NACLs to block “high ports” for compliance. I remember a PR that added explicit denies for ephemeral ranges >49152.
tara-oncall: PR #3421 last night updated nacl for subnet edge-public to deny inbound 49152-65535. Might be that.
jonathan: NACLs are stateless — if the outbound established flow has ephemeral src >49152 then the return packets need inbound allow for that port range. If those are being denied, we'll see exactly this.
keith-infra: Running quick check: ```aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0abc | jq '.NetworkAcls[].Entries'``` shows an explicit DENY for inbound ports 49152-65535 on the edge subnet.
maria-g: But pods are in private subnets behind NAT gateway. Why would edge NACL matter?
keith-infra: NAT gateway resides in the public subnet; it uses ephemeral source ports in that high range. The instance's connection to model registry is SNATed by the NAT GW, so return traffic must be allowed to the NAT's ephemeral ports on the public subnet NACL. The deny is killing the SYN,ACK.
devin-ml: That explains why curl from bastion (in same public subnet) works — bastion not going through the NAT in the same way.
keith-infra: Temporary fix: add NACL allow for ephemeral range 1024-65535 inbound to public subnet and mirror outbound. Applying now via console for quickest rollback, then we'll codify in terraform.
keith-infra: Applied. Re-checking tcpdump: now SYN,ACK reaches NAT and pods get responses.
maria-g: Re-ran model pulls, success. Load drops and SLI returning to normal. Thanks. :thumbsup:
jonathan: Can we get the exact terraform diff so we don't reintroduce this? Also add a test in infra CI that simulates nat egress ephemeral port return path.
tara-oncall: I'll open a follow-up ticket: INFRA-987 add terraform guardrail + runbook for NACL ephemeral ports.
keith-infra: Note for the runbook: avoid deny rules that block ephemeral ports on public subnets with active NAT gateways. Use explicit allow-of-needed-ports + least-privilege elsewhere.
devin-ml: Agree. Also add a monitoring check that alerts when model-puller failure rate > 5% + tcp handshake failure ratio spikes.
opsbot: Incident resolved by keith-infra at 1719876840.
maria-g: Thanks everyone, marking as resolved on our side.
keith-infra: Will follow up with PR to terraform and small postmortem in /postmortems.```
